newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian teens stranded on Arctic ice floe.
newsitem.headline: Canadian teens stranded on Arctic ice floe.

text.p: A group of teenage students and their teachers were stranded on an ice floe on Wednesday in Canada's Arctic after high winds set them adrift on an expedition to learn traditional Eskimo ways.

The 15 people were off the north end of Baffin Island near Canada's border with Greenland. Snow, freezing rain and high winds have hampered rescue efforts so far, said Capt. Joanne Clouatre, a spokeswoman for Canada's military rescue team based in Trenton, Ontario.

The 10 students, aged 16 to 20, and five teachers were setting up camp on the ice on Monday night when high winds and strong currents broke off a chunk of the ice. The floe has now drifted 25 miles (40 km) from shore, Clouatre said.

Most of the group members are Inuit, or Eskimo, from the outpost of Pond Inlet and were taking part in a trip aimed at learning traditional lifestyles and survival skills. They were in good condition and have been in contact with authorities by radio, although their batteries were running low.
"They are doing fine and they have enough supplies to stay there until Friday if they have to," Clouatre said.

A transport plane was scheduled to fly over the group later on Wednesday to evaluate the situation. The floe is only big enough to land a helicopter on and officials hope the weather will improve enough to send one to the area.
